taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts the species with three subspecies. The learner stays at species rank because Hays/Travis/Williamson records span differing subspecific treatments.
look_here_first: Start with the twig tips and leaf underside. Gum bumelia is a shrub or small tree with some short shoots ending in sharp spine-like tips, simple entire leaves, and young foliage that is distinctly woolly or tawny beneath. Older leaves become glossier above while the lower surface stays conspicuously hairy.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays project wild-observation pool + Travis herbarium record within the S. lanuginosum complex + Williamson County subsp. oblongifolium treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Species-level learner retained while local subspecific concepts remain historically variable.

best_field_traits: some short shoots terminate in sharp spine-like tips
young lower leaf surface woolly/tomentose, often tawny
older upper leaf surface glossier and less hairy
small flowers in fascicles from short shoots
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Look for woolly/tawny leaf undersides plus spine-like short shoots on an alternate-leaved woody plant.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Alternate simple entire leaves + woolly/tawny underside + spine-like twig tips is the strongest combination.
